# M1-S4: every logos package implicitly imports logos/rt, including the
# external test package; plain Go packages never do.

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# A loGo/s package can import logos/rt explicitly and run.
cd rt
logos run .
stdout '^rt-ok$'
logos build .

# logos list shows the implicit logos/rt dependency of a .lgo package that
# never names the import (package p has no logos/rt import of its own; the
# explicit importer above is package main).
logos list -f '{{.Deps}}' ./p
stdout 'logos/rt'

# The external test build passes: the p_test package resolves and runs.
logos test ./...
stdout 'ok\s+example\.com/rt/p'

# The external p_test package of a .lgo package carries logos/rt in its
# own dependency list (not just via the base package).
logos list -test -f '{{.ImportPath}} {{.Deps}}' ./...
stdout 'example\.com/rt/p_test \[example\.com/rt/p\.test\] \[.*logos/rt.*\]'

# Plain Go packages never gain the import, under either command.
cd ../gomod
go list -deps .
! stdout 'logos/rt'
logos list -deps .
! stdout 'logos/rt'

-- rt/go.mod --
module example.com/rt

go 1.27

-- rt/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"logos/rt"
)

func main() {
	rt.Cold()
	fmt.Println("rt-ok")
}

-- rt/p/p.lgo --
package p

func Msg() string { return "p-ok" }

-- rt/p/p_test.lgo --
package p_test

import "testing"

func TestExternal(t *testing.T) {
	if 1+1 != 2 {
		t.Fatal("unreachable")
	}
}

-- gomod/go.mod --
module example.com/goplain

go 1.27

-- gomod/main.go --
package main

import "fmt"

func main() { fmt.Println("go-ok") }
